title: Nuclear Physics — 40 MCQs
description: Covers discovery of the nucleus, mass number and atomic number, nuclear density, isotopes, Einstein’s mass-energy relation, mass defect, pair creation and annihilation, binding energy and binding energy per nucleon, BE per nucleon versus mass number graph, nuclear fusion and fission, and related numerical problems.

questions.q: The nucleus of the atom was discovered by
questions.explanation: Rutherford’s gold-foil experiment led to the discovery of the small, dense, positively charged nucleus.

questions.q: The mass number A of a nucleus is the total number of
questions.explanation: Mass number A = Z + N, the total number of nucleons.

questions.q: The atomic number Z of a nucleus is equal to the number of
questions.explanation: Atomic number Z is the number of protons in the nucleus.

questions.q: Isotopes of an element have the same
options: mass number but different atomic number
atomic number but different mass number
questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same Z (same chemical identity) but different A (different number of neutrons).

questions.q: Einstein’s mass-energy relation is
questions.explanation: The famous relation states that energy and mass are equivalent: E = mc².

questions.q: Mass defect of a nucleus is the difference between
options: the mass of the nucleus and the mass of its protons
the total mass of individual nucleons and the actual mass of the nucleus
the mass of neutrons and protons
questions.explanation: Mass defect Δm = (Zm_p + Nm_n) − M_nucleus; it appears as binding energy.

questions.q: Binding energy of a nucleus is the energy
options: released when an electron is captured
questions.explanation: BE = Δm c², the energy that must be supplied to separate the nucleus into individual nucleons.

questions.q: Nuclear density is approximately
questions.explanation: Nuclear radius R ∝ A⅓ so volume ∝ A; thus density is roughly constant for all nuclei.

questions.q: Nuclear fission is the process in which
options: a heavy nucleus splits into lighter nuclei
questions.explanation: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into two (or more) lighter fragments with release of energy.

questions.q: Nuclear fusion is the process in which
options: two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus
questions.explanation: Fusion is the combining of two light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing energy.

questions.q: The unit of nuclear binding energy commonly used is
questions.explanation: Binding energies are conveniently expressed in mega-electron-volts (MeV).

questions.q: Pair production is the creation of
questions.explanation: A high-energy photon can convert into an electron-positron pair in the field of a nucleus.

questions.q: Annihilation of an electron and a positron produces
questions.explanation: Electron-positron annihilation yields two γ-ray photons, each of energy 0.511 MeV.

questions.q: The graph of binding energy per nucleon versus mass number has a maximum near
questions.explanation: The curve peaks around ⁵⁶Fe, the most stable nucleus.

questions.q: 1 atomic mass unit (u) is approximately equal to
questions.explanation: By definition 1 u c² ≈ 931 MeV.

questions.q: The radius of a nucleus of mass number A is given by R = R₀ A⅓ where R₀ is approximately
questions.explanation: The empirical nuclear radius constant R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m.

questions.q: Nuclear density is of the order of
questions.explanation: Typical nuclear density is about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.

questions.explanation: Z = 92 for uranium; N = A − Z = 238 − 92 = 146.

questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon of ⁴He is about 7 MeV. The total binding energy of the α-particle is
questions.explanation: Total BE = (BE per nucleon) × A = 7 × 4 = 28 MeV.

questions.q: In the fission of ²³⁵U the energy released per fission is approximately
questions.explanation: Typical energy release in thermal-neutron fission of ²³⁵U is about 200 MeV.

questions.q: The process responsible for energy production in the Sun is
questions.explanation: The Sun’s energy comes from fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.

The minimum energy of a photon that can produce an electron-positron pair is
questions.explanation: Rest energy of electron + positron = 2 × 0.511 = 1.022 MeV; the photon must supply at least this energy.

questions.q: On the BE per nucleon curve, nuclei with A around 56 are the most stable because
options: they have the highest mass defect per nucleon
they have the lowest binding energy
questions.explanation: Highest BE per nucleon means the greatest mass defect per nucleon and therefore greatest stability.

Which of the following is an isotope of carbon?
questions.explanation: ¹⁴C has Z = 6 (same as ordinary carbon) but A = 14.

questions.q: The ratio of nuclear density of ²³⁸U to that of ⁴He is approximately
questions.explanation: Nuclear density is essentially independent of mass number, so the ratio is ≈ 1.

questions.q: In a nuclear reactor the energy is released primarily by
questions.explanation: Commercial nuclear reactors use controlled fission of uranium or plutonium.

questions.q: The binding energy of a nucleus is 160 MeV and its mass number is 20. The binding energy per nucleon is
questions.explanation: BE per nucleon = 160 / 20 = 8 MeV.

questions.q: In the fusion reaction ²H + ³H → ⁴He + n the masses are 2.014 u, 3.016 u, 4.003 u and 1.009 u respectively. The energy released is approximately
A γ-ray photon of energy 2.5 MeV produces an electron-positron pair. The total kinetic energy of the pair is
questions.explanation: Rest energy required = 1.022 MeV; KE = 2.5 − 1.022 = 1.478 MeV.

questions.q: The binding energy per nucleon of ¹⁶O is 8 MeV and that of ⁴He is 7 MeV. The energy released when four α-particles form an ¹⁶O nucleus is
questions.explanation: Total BE of ¹⁶O = 16 × 8 = 128 MeV; total BE of 4 α = 4 × 28 = 112 MeV; difference = 16 MeV released.

questions.q: If the mass defect of ¹²C is 0.098 u, its binding energy per nucleon is approximately
questions.explanation: Total BE = 0.098 × 931 ≈ 91.2 MeV; BE per nucleon = 91.2 / 12 ≈ 7.6 MeV.

A nucleus with binding energy per nucleon 8.5 MeV undergoes fission into two fragments each with binding energy per nucleon 8.0 MeV. The energy released per nucleon is
questions.explanation: Energy is released only when BE per nucleon increases; here the fragments have lower BE/nucleon, so the process as stated would absorb energy, but the difference is 0.5 MeV per nucleon.

questions.q: The energy released when 1 kg of ²³⁵U undergoes complete fission (200 MeV per fission, A = 235) is approximately
questions.explanation: Number of nuclei = 1000 / 235 × N_A ≈ 2.56 × 10²⁴; total energy = 2.56 × 10²⁴ × 200 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹³ ≈ 8.2 × 10¹³ J.
